I did not take the verifier's word: I pulled the Project Gutenberg 5740 LaTeX source (https://www.gutenberg.org/files/5740/5740-t/5740-t.tex) to disk and read proposition 5.6 in both languages myself. English, macro PropositionE 5.6: “The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.” German, macro PropositionG 5.6: “Die Grenzen meiner Sprache bedeuten die Grenzen meiner Welt.” Word for word, stop included. The PG metadata names Ogden as translator and the file's own front matter names Kegan Paul, Trench, Trubner and Harcourt Brace, 1922, so the edition and year in the source line are right. Translation drift, this track's usual kill, is not available here: Pears and McGuinness render 5.6 identically, so there is no rival wording to confuse. The locator is the proposition number, which is how the Tractatus is cited. Shipped.js: not shipped, no near miss, Wittgenstein at 0 of 3, not banned. In scope: philosophy, 1922, no content warning, no speaker to name. Source line leads with the name, 95 characters, and the only dash in it is the hyphen inside Logico-Philosophicus, which is a title's own spelling and not the em dash rule 5 forbids. Tag Philosophy is the form of the work. Two small inaccuracies in the verifier's evidence prose, neither touching the citation: the PG e-book does not set the German facing the English, its front matter says it was reformatted to put the whole English translation first and the German after, and the original 1922 parallel setting is what had German on even pages; and the file is a LaTeX source, not a scan. The citation stands as written. One optional note for the editor, not a defect: Ogden italicises “The limits of my language”, which a card cannot show.
